title: H.S. Code Tariff Classification and Duty Adjustment
summary: This thread tracks the continuous refinement of the Bangladesh Customs Tariff schedule. It involves the systematic replacement, insertion, and deletion of H.S. Codes to ensure accurate commodity classification, duty rate adjustments, and the implementation of specific tax exemptions for industrial raw materials and finished goods.

evolution.structure: Shifted from simple code replacement to complex, sector-specific duty exemption tables.
evolution.procedure: Increased emphasis on VAT-registration and local manufacturing status as prerequisites for code-based duty concessions.

timeline.change: Initial series of code substitutions and deletions for tariff alignment.
Updates to classification codes and expansion of product descriptions under existing codes.
Systematic replacement of codes and introduction of pre-shipment inspection exemptions based on duty rates.
Introduction of duty concessions for specific equipment and further code refinements.
Extensive updates to tariff tables, including code substitutions, deletions, and specific duty rate adjustments.
Major overhaul of classification codes for industrial inputs and pharmaceutical ingredients.
Consolidation of tariff tables and introduction of specific duty exemptions for local manufacturing sectors.
Refinement of industrial raw material classifications and formalization of documentation requirements for H.S. Code declarations.

Customs Act 1969: This act serves as the legal framework, specifically under section 19(1), for granting customs duty and supplementary duty exemptions on imported goods.
National Board of Revenue: The Government issued this order in consultation with the National Board of Revenue to provide specific duty exemptions on industrial raw materials.
Customs Duty: This order establishes specific reduced rates for customs duty on various raw materials imported by VAT-registered manufacturing industries as listed in the associated tables.
Supplementary Duty: This order defines the supplementary duty exemptions applicable to industrial imports, setting specific rates for goods listed in the provided tables to incentivize local manufacturing.
Imported Raw Materials: A wide range of industrial inputs, categorized by H.S. Code, are granted duty concessions when imported by VAT-registered manufacturing industries for production purposes.
TABLE-1: This table lists essential industrial inputs eligible for zero-rated customs and supplementary duties when imported by designated VAT-registered manufacturing industries.
TABLE-2: This table identifies various chemical and industrial components subject to a five percent customs duty rate when imported by authorized VAT-registered domestic manufacturers.
TABLE-3: This table specifies industrial raw materials that qualify for a ten percent customs duty rate upon importation by registered manufacturing industries.
TABLE-4: This table outlines specific materials and components, such as seasoning mixes and fire-resistant door parts, subject to a fifteen percent customs duty rate for registered industrial importers.
TABLE-5: This table identifies specialized industrial parts and materials, including footwear components and refrigerator parts, eligible for a twenty-five percent customs duty rate.
